title: Drone Scare Shuts Amritsar Airspace, Diverting Three Incoming Flights
excerpt: Two to three drones spotted near Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport on the night of October 11 forced authorities to close the airspace for about 90 minutes; three flights were diverted and police suspect the drones were filming a kabaddi tournament.
body:
• On the night of October 11, two to three drones were spotted near Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport around 9:30–9:40 pm; CISF personnel alerted air traffic control and the airspace was closed at about 9:50 pm.
  • Three incoming flights were diverted: Air India AI-855 (Delhi) was sent back to Delhi, IndiGo 6E-5028 (Mumbai) was routed to Chandigarh — landing around 10:30 pm and departing again for Amritsar at 11:25 pm — and Malaysia Airlines MH-118 (Kuala Lumpur) was diverted to Delhi. Flight operations resumed between 10:30 and 11:15 pm.
  • What this means for you: if you are flying into Amritsar this month, check your flight status with the airline before leaving for the airport, keep your phone on for rebooking alerts, and leave buffer time for onward travel into Punjab — a diversion puts you down in Delhi or Chandigarh, several hours away by road. Rebook in the airline’s app or at its transfer desk at the airport you land in rather than waiting at the information counter.
  • Preliminary police findings suggest the drones were filming a kabaddi tournament in a nearby village; flying drones is prohibited within an 8-km radius of the airport. A similar scare in September forced seven flights to divert.

A drone scare shut down the airspace over Amritsar’s Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport for roughly 90 minutes on the night of October 11, forcing three incoming flights to divert and leaving passengers stranded in a city that is one of Punjab’s busiest gateways. The airspace was closed around 9:50 pm after information was received about the movement of two to three drones near the airport, and operations resumed between 10:30 and 11:15 pm following a security review.

"A similar scare in September forced seven flights to divert."

Context & Background

Amritsar airport sits in a high-security zone in a border state, which is why even a brief unidentified-drone sighting triggers a full closure. Airport officials said Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel stationed at the airport reported the objects at high altitude around 9:30 pm and alerted the control room as a precaution.

A preliminary police investigation indicated the drones may have been flown to videograph a sports tournament — reportedly a kabaddi competition — in a nearby village, the Times of India reported. But drone operations are prohibited within an eight-kilometre radius of the airport, regardless of intent. Amritsar Rural SSP Kanwalpreet Singh Chahal said police teams were deployed in nearby villages and a search operation was under way to establish the nature of the drone activity. Police appealed to residents not to fly drones without permission.

This is the second such incident in about a month. In September, as many as five suspected drones were spotted near the airport, forcing seven commercial flights to divert to Delhi and Chandigarh. A preliminary inquiry then also pointed to drones being used during a sports tournament in a nearby village — suggesting the compliance problem, not the hardware, is the recurring issue.

Impact & Analysis

The disruption hit all three diverted flights hard. Air India’s AI-855, arriving from Delhi, was sent back to the national capital. IndiGo’s 6E-5028, arriving from Mumbai, was rerouted to Chandigarh, where it landed around 10:30 pm and took off again for Amritsar at 11:25 pm. Malaysia Airlines flight MH-118 from Kuala Lumpur was diverted to Delhi, according to local reporting.

Several passengers were left stranded, and some reportedly protested over the lack of information from officials — a reminder that the operational response, not just the security response, shapes how these scares feel on the ground. Unlike the September episode, this time most aircraft were back moving within the hour after the Joint Action Committee’s security review concluded.

Diaspora Angle

Amritsar is a major arrival point for the diaspora: family visits to Punjab and pilgrimages to the Golden Temple route heavily through this airport, and October marks the start of the busy winter travel season. If your flight gets diverted, head to the airline’s transfer desk at the airport you land in — or rebook directly in the airline’s app, where inventory updates faster than at the counter — and confirm your onward transport before you clear the terminal, since Delhi and Chandigarh are each several hours from Amritsar by road.

What’s Next

Police have deployed teams in villages around the airport to trace the drones and determine who flew them; further action will depend on the investigation’s findings. With two scares in a month traced to the same apparent cause, authorities face a straightforward enforcement question: how to make the 8-km no-drone rule around the airport stick in the surrounding villages before a third scare grounds flights again.

Sources: The Times of India, Daily Kiran
